title: Preservation on the proved finite-Tor domains
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ range over separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use bounded constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], its cohomological intervals [def-weil-constructible-intervals], finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
At this finite coefficient stage the following hold:

1. **(i)** $Lf^*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
1. **(ii)** Derived tensor carries
$D^b_{ctf}\times D^b_{ctf}$ into $D^b_{ctf}$; if the two inputs have
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, the output has Tor amplitude in
$[a+c,b+d]$.
For $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, internal Hom also belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
If $K,L$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ and
$m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $\dim X\leq m$, then $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ has Tor amplitude in
$[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$; if moreover $K$ is site-perfect, it has Tor
amplitude in the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$.
The elementary formula $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$
with coefficient dual $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,A_X)$, and the
dimension-free interval $[c-b,d-a]$, still require
a site-perfect first argument (for the origin
$i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$, both $i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor
amplitude $[0,0]$, while $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*A(-1)[-2]$ has
cohomology in degree $2$);
the general preservation assertion uses geometric Verdier duality.
1. **(iii)** $Rf_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$; for input Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ and
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $\dim X\leq d$, the output has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
1. **(iv)** $Rf_!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
1. **(v)** The exceptional adjoint on the constructible
coefficient category satisfies $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$ and carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
For nonnegative integer dimension bounds $d_X,d_Y$ with
$\dim X\leq d_X$ and $\dim Y\leq d_Y$
[def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and input Tor interval $[a,b]$,
one output interval is $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$.
For nonempty schemes the bounds may be their dimensions;
for an empty scheme the bound may be zero.
1. **(vi)** For every separated finite-type $X/k$,
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(-,Ra_X^!A)$ is a contravariant exact
anti-equivalence with $K\simeq D_XD_XK$, by the geometric
Verdier-biduality theorem on this domain.
1. **(vii)** On the finite-Tor constructible domains,
finite coefficient quotients commute with pullback, tensor, both
direct images, general internal Hom, Verdier duality and the
exceptional adjoint, preserving their evaluation and adjunction maps.
For derived-complete
integral objects, $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
General internal Hom and the exceptional adjoint preserve this
category; Verdier duality is an anti-equivalence on it, with the
canonical finite reductions of these operations. These conclusions
pass to the bounded constructible categories at $E$ and
$\Qlb$, with their specified coefficient-passage operations.
The elementary site-perfect formula in (ii) retains its stated
hypothesis. No unrestricted unbounded pro-etale exceptional
adjunction is asserted here.

proof.text: For (i), [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives bounded constructibility and the unchanged Tor interval $[a,b]$ for the separated finite-type morphism $f$. For the tensor assertion of (ii), [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) gives bounded constructibility and Tor interval $[a+c,b+d]$. These are precisely membership in the finite-Tor subcategories of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For the site-perfect formula in (ii), apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] on the chosen small coefficient site, with ring sheaf $A_X$. Site-perfectness in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] is exactly its local bounded finite-free-retract hypothesis. Its canonical evaluation isomorphism gives $K^\vee\otimes^L_A L\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$, with $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,A_X)$. This uses ringed-site duality, without assuming a six-functor datum.

To prove the sharper Tor bound, [lem-sf-site-perfect-tor-window] applied to $K$ gives, on a covering of each site object, finite-projective models $P$ supported in $[a,b]$. This node supplies both restriction of the Tor condition to arbitrary slice test sheaves and shortening of the perfect model to these precise degrees. Use these models in the following two steps.

source.place: paragraph 1, choosing a local perfect model in the prescribed interval

proof.text: Each functor $\mathcal Hom_A(P^r,-)$ is a retract of a finite sum of identity functors, hence is exact. By [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] the map $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,A_X[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I(A_X[0]))$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The latter represents the derived dual by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Thus the ordinary dual represents $K^\vee$ on this slice, using the restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. By the degree formula of [def-pur-hom-complex], its degree $r$ term is $(P^{-r})^\vee$. It vanishes outside $[-b,-a]$ and is a finite-free retract, by dualizing the given retraction maps.

source.place: paragraph 1, reversed degrees of the local dual

proof.text: Finite-free retracts are flat: their tensor functors are retracts of finite sums of the identity. The bounded dual of the preceding step is therefore K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Choose for $L$ a flat model supported in $[c,d]$ by [lem-sf-flat-model]; restriction to the covering slices is exact and monoidal by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], so it preserves flatness. [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes the dual tensor by the total tensor of these models. Its terms are flat and vanish outside $[c-b,d-a]$. Tensoring it with a degree-zero test sheaf has the same degree bounds, so the evaluation isomorphism in Step 2 gives this Tor bound locally. Sheaf cohomology vanishing is local, giving the asserted bound globally.

source.place: paragraph 1, tensoring the reversed dual interval

proof.text: For arbitrary $K,L$ in the finite-Tor constructible category, [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] gives bounded constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, and the interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$ on either site. Its hypotheses are satisfied because $X$ is separated and finite type and $m$ is a nonnegative dimension bound. This proves the general internal-Hom assertion; the preceding steps give its site-perfect refinement.

For the origin $i:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_k$, work first on the etale site. [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] gives stalk $A$ at the origin and zero elsewhere for $i_*A$. Exact and conservative geometric stalks, [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], together with [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], show that tensoring with $i_*A$ preserves injections. Thus $i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor interval $[0,0]$. The canonical comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] identifies $\nu^*Ri_*A$ with $Ri_*\nu^*A$; etale exactness of $i_*$ follows from the same stalk formula. [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) therefore gives the same two Tor intervals for the pro-etale sheaves, where $i_*$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] since its complement is quasi-compact.

source.place: paragraph 1, flatness of the origin example

proof.text: On the pro-etale site of the Noetherian $\mathbf A^1_k$, specialize [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] to $s=i$ and $P=M=A$: $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)\cong Ri_*Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A$, with $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}$ the right adjoint of $i_*$ on the ambient unbounded categories. This is not by definition the constructible functor $Ri^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; compare them. With $j:\mathbf G_{m,k}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_k$, [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle] gives a triangle $i_*Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\to A\to Rj_*j^*A\to$. By [prop-sf-localization-all-stages](1'),(3') at $\Lambda=A$, the last two vertices lie in $D^b_{ctf}$, triangulated by [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated], hence so does the first. The counit $i^*i_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is invertible by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] and $i^*$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ by (3'), so $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\in D^b_c(\operatorname{Spec}k,A)$. For $Q$ there, the ambient adjunction and clause (2) give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Ri^!A)$; Yoneda gives $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\cong Ri^!A$. [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] with $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $c=1$ states $Ri^!A\cong A(-1)[-2]$ for every $n\geq1$. Exactness [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] gives $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)\cong i_*A(-1)[-2]$. Its degree-two cohomology is nonzero: the rank-one twist is nonzero and $i_*$ is fully faithful by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. This holds for ramified $E$ and every $n$.

source.place: paragraph 1, purity and supported Hom in the origin example

proof.text: For (iii), [lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] supplies UDV(f,A;2d): the coefficient ring is finite, killed by a power of ell, and ell is invertible in k. Applying [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] with N=2d proves the etale assertion, and [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] proves the assertion for every bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale input. For (iv), the finite-type separated target is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies f=pj with j open and p proper. The middle scheme is finite type over k because p is proper over the finite-type target. By [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], the compact-support candidate is Rp_*j_!. By [lem-trf-open-ctf], j_! preserves bounded constructibility and the Tor interval, and (iii) applied to p gives preservation for the candidate. Every input in the statement is of etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] identifies this candidate with the specified compact-support functor independently of the compactification.

For (v), a closed immersion i:Z\hookrightarrow T with dim T<=d has quasi-compact open complement because T is Noetherian. By [thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional] its complement has all-sheaf vanishing and constructible direct images with c=2d; these are exactly the hypotheses of [prop-exc-closed-tor], giving Tor interval [a,b+2d+1]. For a smooth separated finite-type map of pure relative dimension r, [cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] gives preservation and interval [a-2r,b-2r]. Choose the finite affine chart presentations U\hookrightarrow A^{d_U}_V of [thm-pur-general-admissibility]. Its open-complement hypotheses are discharged by [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum]. Explicitly, for X nonempty take D=max d_U and c_U=2(d_U+dim Y). Each expression c_U+1+2(D-d_U) equals 2D+2dim Y+1, so the assembled interval is [a-2D,b+2dim Y+1]. For X empty the chart family is empty and the output is zero. In the pro-etale constructible category [thm-sf-preservation-class](2) states this preservation for every separated finite-type f, with no unrestricted ambient adjoint assumption. The formula in [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identifies this exceptional functor with D_X Lf^* D_Y. To obtain the sharper bound stated in the item, apply [cor-coef-finite-verdier] with the identity quotient $A\to A$: on a scheme of dimension at most e, D sends [u,v] to [-v-2e,-u]. Thus D_Y sends [a,b] to [-b-2d_Y,-a]; (i) leaves this interval unchanged; D_X then sends it to [a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]. If X or Y is empty, the exceptional output is zero, so any nonnegative dimension bounds give a valid interval. For (vi), [thm-fix-general-biduality] gives the exact contravariant anti-equivalence and the canonical biduality isomorphism on either finite-coefficient site.

For (vii), fix a quotient $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with 1<=m<=n. On the finite-Tor domains [lem-fix-operation-reduction] gives the pullback, tensor and compact-support comparisons and their tensor, evaluation, unit and counit compatibilities. For ordinary direct image, [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] gives the counit-defined comparison, its naturality and its coefficient-quotient cocycle; for a pro-etale input K, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) gives a bounded constructible etale representative K′ with K isomorphic to nu_T^*K′, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives K′ the same finite Tor interval as K. Thus both the constructibility and finite-Tor hypotheses of its pro-etale assertion hold. For general internal Hom use the evaluation-defined comparison of [thm-coef-finite-hom], which explicitly respects evaluation and tensor-Hom adjunction and needs no site-perfect first variable. For Verdier duality, [cor-coef-finite-verdier] gives the quotient cocycle and compatibility with evaluation and biduality. For the exceptional functor, [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] gives the quotient cocycle and identifies the units and counits under compact-support coefficient change. These are the specified comparison maps, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of the resulting objects.

For a derived-complete integral input $K$, its residue reduction $K_1$ has cohomology in some finite interval. [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives that same Tor interval for every canonical reduction $K_n$ and explicitly concludes $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$. For integral $K,L$, [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] gives preservation by ambient internal Hom and a uniform reduction interval; [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] identifies its canonical finite reductions and evaluations. [thm-coef-integral-verdier] supplies the exact duality anti-equivalence, its canonical reductions and biduality. These nodes supply the integral assertions directly.

source.place: paragraph 5, integral residue, internal Hom and Verdier duality

proof.text: For the integral exceptional operation, apply [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] with $R=\mathcal O_E$ to the given separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$. Its statement specifies the coherent normalized tower before the total inverse limit and gives the functor $G_fL=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_n^!L_n$. It states preservation, the right adjunction to integral $Rf_!$, the identification $G_fL\cong D_{X,R}f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}D_{Y,R}L$, and the canonical reductions $(G_fL)_n\cong Rf_n^!L_n$ identifying actual units and counits. A uniform input Tor interval $[a,b]$ exists by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]; the same exceptional-adjoint statement gives the output interval $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$ for nonnegative dimension bounds, including bound zero for an empty scheme. No construction or effectivity of an arbitrary levelwise tower is used here.

source.place: paragraph 5, specified coherent integral exceptional adjunction

proof.text: At $E$, [thm-coef-rational-verdier] gives rationalized evaluation and biduality and the finite-field-extension cocycle; [lem-coef-rational-operations] identifies internal Hom and the exceptional functor with the specified coefficient-passage operations, preserving evaluations, units and counits. [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] then states that these compatible finite-field functors induce the common-stage duality and exceptional adjunction, including compatibility with retracts. In particular its explicit formula $(E,K)\mapsto(E,D_{X,E}K)$ supplies the common-stage representative; its assertion about retracts supplies the extension to the idempotent completion. These are applications of the existing coefficient-passage theorems, with no new descent argument hidden in this step.

source.place: paragraph 5, rationalization and common-stage coefficient passage

proof.text:
For (i), bounded constructibility is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible], and
flat inverse image in [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat]
preserves the Tor interval of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
For (ii), the Tor intervals add under derived tensor: with bounded
flat models of $K$ in $[a,b]$ and of $L$ in $[c,d]$, the total tensor
complex is a bounded flat model in $[a+c,b+d]$. Refine the
finite constructible stratifications for the two complexes; the
bounded tensor complexes on each stratum have finite locally constant
cohomology, which gives constructibility. If $K$ is site-perfect
in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], a bounded finite-projective
local model $P$ in $[a,b]$ computes its dual and identifies
$R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$ by
[prop-sf-dualizable-hom]. The tensor argument proves Hom
preservation in that case, and since $P^\vee$ is a bounded
finite-projective complex in $[-b,-a]$, the tensor bound gives the
interval $[c-b,d-a]$; this is the sharper assertion of
[thm-sf-hom-ctf], whose argument is local on the site and so applies
on either site; on the pro-étale site this is [cor-sf-hom-ctf-proetale-unconditional]. For a general constructible finite-Tor
first argument, use [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom], whose
proof uses geometric Verdier biduality and gives the
dimension-dependent interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. The displayed
example shows the dimension-free interval fails without
site-perfectness: $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*Ri^!A$ by adjunction, and
$Ri^!A=A(-1)[-2]$ by purity for the point in the smooth curve.

Clause (iii) is [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]: its etale
calculation is [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the
uniform all-sheaf cohomological bound supplied by
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]. That calculation uses a
bounded-above free resolution of a finite constant coefficient and
the cohomological bound; it does not use a projection formula for an
arbitrary sheaf on the target. For (iv), choose a compactification
$f=pj$ and use [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].
Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact and commutes with tensor, as is
seen on stalks, so preserves the Tor interval and constructibility.
Apply (iii) to the proper factor $p$.

Clause (v) is the preservation result for the exceptional inverse
image, assembled from the closed and smooth cases. For a closed immersion
$i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $\dim T\leq d$, the open complement satisfies
the open-complement condition with $c=2d$ by
[thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional], so [prop-exc-closed-tor]
carries bounded constructible input of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ to bounded
constructible output of Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d+1]$. For $f$ smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$, purity identifies $Rf^!$ with $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and
[cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] gives the shift $-2d$ on both intervals.
A general $f$ is, on affine charts $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, a closed
immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ followed by the smooth
projection, and composing the two cases along the charts is
[thm-pur-general-admissibility]; its open-complement hypothesis on the
charts is discharged by [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum], so it is a
theorem and not an assumption. At the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$ and for every
separated finite-type $f$ of the statement this is
[thm-sf-preservation-class](2): $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with no ambient datum assumed on that category. With this
preservation, the finite dual formula and adjunction of
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identify $Rf^!$ with $D_Xf^*D_Y$ on this
domain; applying the finite duality bound on $Y$, ordinary pullback, and
the finite duality bound on $X$ gives the displayed output interval. Clause (vi) is
[thm-fix-general-biduality] at finite coefficients;
its geometric proof supplies the
anti-equivalence and is not replaced by the site-perfect calculation
in (ii).

For (vii), use [lem-fix-operation-reduction] for pullback,
tensor and compact supports, and [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]
for ordinary direct image. General finite internal-Hom and duality
comparisons are [thm-coef-finite-hom], [cor-coef-finite-verdier];
the exceptional comparison is [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].
Their proofs compare the specified evaluations and adjunction maps.

At integral coefficients, [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]
identifies the two constructible categories. General internal Hom
and its finite reductions are
[cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction].
The anti-equivalence and exceptional adjunction are
[thm-coef-integral-verdier], [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint].
These proofs establish normalized-tower effectivity and the finite
reductions with uniform bounds; they do not infer a common integral
local model merely from levelwise constructibility.
Finally [thm-coef-rational-verdier], [lem-coef-rational-operations]
identify the operations after rationalization, and
[thm-coef-qbar-verdier] transports them to the common-stage
category, including its retracts. Their adjunctions have precisely
the bounded constructible domains stated in those results.
